Earnings Call Transcript
Goosehead (GSHD) Q4 2025 Earnings Call Transcript
By

Motley Fool Transcribing

–

Feb 21, 2026 at 12:18AM EST




Image source: The Motley Fool.


DATE
Tuesday, Feb. 17, 2026 at 4:30 p.m. ET
CALL PARTICIPANTS
President and Chief Executive Officer — Mark K. Miller
Chief Financial Officer and Chief Operating Officer — Mark Jones Jr.
Vice President, Investor Relations — Daniel D. Farrell
TAKEAWAYS
Total Revenue
-- $105,300,000 for the quarter, up 12% year over year, and $365,300,000 for the year, up 16%.
Core Revenue
-- $78,200,000 for the quarter, up 15%, and $317,900,000 for the year, up 16%.
Total Written Premiums
-- $1,100,000,000 for the quarter, up 13%, and $4,400,000,000 for the year, up 17%.
Franchise Premiums
-- $896,000,000 for the quarter, up 15%.
Corporate Premiums
-- $194,000,000 for the quarter, up 4%.
Policies in Force
-- 1,900,000 at year-end, increasing 14%, with accelerated growth from 13% in the previous quarter.
Client Retention
-- Improved sequentially, ending the year above the prior quarter's 85%.
Adjusted EBITDA
-- $39,200,000 for the quarter, up 5%; $113,600,000 for the year, up 14%, with a 31% margin.
Gross Payments per Franchise
-- Up 29% year over year, reflecting higher cash flow for franchise owners.
Producers per Franchise
-- Increased from 1.9 to 2.1 year over year.
Same Store Sales (Franchise Network)
-- Grew 19% in the quarter.
Corporate Sales Agent Headcount
-- Reached 374 at year-end, up 6%.
Enterprise Sales/Partnership Headcount
-- Increased nearly 100% to 115 at year-end; partners now address 2,300,000 potential clients.
Technology Investment
-- Technology now accounts for the largest expense line, focused on expansion of the Digital Agent 2.0 platform and AI-based tools.
Digital Agent 2.0 Platform
-- Now live in Texas with multiple home and auto carriers and true end-to-end binding capability.
Strategic Investments
-- $2,900,000 incurred in the quarter; 2026 forecast is $25,000,000–$35,000,000 in total, with $8,000,000–$11,000,000 to the P&L.
Contingent Commissions
-- $25,300,000 in the quarter; $41,100,000 for the year, representing 86 basis points of total written premiums.
Cash Flow from Operations
-- $91,800,000 for the year, up 28%.
Cash and Cash Equivalents
-- $34,400,000 at year-end; Total debt: $298,500,000.
Share Repurchase
-- 323,000 shares bought in the quarter ($22,500,000); $81,700,000 for the year, totaling nearly 8% of Class A shares since 2024.
2026 Guidance
-- Organic total revenue growth expected at 10%-19%; organic written premium growth between 12%-20%.
Texas Premium Mix
-- Texas accounted for 38% of fourth quarter premium and 40% of full-year premium, with a stated plan for further geographic diversification.
Partnership Implementation
-- Majority of the 2,300,000 partner-client base remains in implementation phase; revenue acceleration expected as these come online.
Net Promoter Score (NPS)
-- Lower than in recent quarters, attributed to broader market pricing; trailing 12-month metric context provided.
Franchise Consolidation
-- Operating franchises decreased from 1,103 to 1,009, while producer count increased from 2,092 to 2,113, demonstrating consolidation among productive agencies.

RISKS
Jones Jr. warned that, "we expect margins to be modestly down as we invest in broadening our app application of AI, as I discussed, and our Digital Agent two point o and partnerships platform," indicating near-term margin compression due to increased technology spending.
Management cautioned that contingent commissions are expected to decline to 60–85 basis points of total written premium in 2026, down from 86 basis points in 2025, reflecting more cautious projections due to inherent variability.
Consolidation of single-producer franchises is expected to "results in a short term revenue impact," though management states it should benefit long-term efficiency.
Management highlighted that the majority of the partnership pipeline is still in implementation, with corresponding benefits "not yet felt in our financial results," making growth projections dependent on successful partner activation.
SUMMARY
Goosehead Insurance

(
GSHD

1.27%
)
reported double-digit growth across total revenue, core revenues, written premiums, and policies in force, driven by increasing productivity in both its franchise and corporate sales networks. The company accelerated technology investments—particularly in its Digital Agent 2.0 and AI-enabled service platforms—while also executing major share repurchases and further diversifying its premium mix by expanding outside Texas. Management provided 2026 guidance reflecting organic revenue growth of 10%-19% and written premiums expanding at 12%-20%, with near-term margin compression expected as technology initiatives scale and partnership channels are implemented. Client retention continued improving sequentially, and headcount gains in both agent and enterprise channels underline expansion in distribution reach.
Technology is now the largest expense line, and management stated that future growth in both franchise and partnership channels depends on successful digital implementation and AI integration.
Despite current lower margins, Jones Jr. asserted, "we're pretty confident that long term and at scale, this is very accretive to the margin profile," emphasizing confidence in strategic investment payoffs beyond 2026.
Share repurchase activity was substantial; $81,700,000 was used in 2025, and a new $180,000,000 buyback authorization was announced amid continued market volatility.
The Texas share of written premiums continues to decrease as the company grows presence in diverse geographies, reducing historical concentration risk.
INDUSTRY GLOSSARY
Contingent Commissions
: Performance-based payments from insurance carriers that are contingent upon meeting certain volume, profitability, or growth targets within an agency's book of business.
Policies in Force
: The total number of active insurance policies held by clients at a given point in time.
Digital Agent 2.0
: Goosehead's proprietary digital distribution platform enabling end-to-end binding of policies without human intervention, aimed at increasing efficiency and client choice.
Franchise Consolidation
: The process by which smaller franchise agencies are acquired by larger, more productive agencies within the Goosehead network, resulting in fewer operating franchises but higher overall productivity per agency.
